searchText: Concurrent requests for historical envelopes can DoS the attached EL under a 8GB working memory assumption. Can test it against a higher resource limit if this is worth the effort. The tokening system sort of works but it is possible to trick it. For example, more than 128 requests from a peer are negatively peer scored but since checking of the currently issued requests happens after a small delay on RPC admission, race conditions exist where more than 128 requests could be admitted. Also, repeated RPCs each exercizing a maximum of 128 envelopes are possible before the peer gets banned, and in this time interval, the attached EL may run out of memory in the process of payload reconstruction hmm probably this should be moved outside of this channel then, I can't think why this issue would be different than Fulu with blocks

excerpts.content:
Concurrent requests for historical envelopes can DoS the attached EL under a 8GB working memory assumption. Can test it against a higher resource limit if this is worth the effort.

The tokening system sort of works but it is possible to trick it. For example, more than 128 requests from a peer are negatively peer scored but since checking of the currently issued requests happens after a small delay on RPC admission, race conditions exist where more than 128 requests could be admitted. Also, repeated RPCs each exercizing a maximum of 128 envelopes are possible before the peer gets banned, and in this time interval, the attached EL may run out of memory in the process of payload reconstruction
